name: level1-lose-revolt
description: Level 1 losing scenario: worker revolt from an unsustainable drilling operation. #553 flips this file's own pre-#553 finding: previously wellBeing could never crash here because a drill_plan wrote holes into state.drillHoles instantly and none of this file's employees were ever physically dispatched anywhere. Now drill_hole is a queued action a driller must physically drive a drill_rig to, and the file's own opening (`vehicle driver 1 1`, required so the free staffed rig is 'actually crewed') is what dooms it: vehicle #1 spawns at (0,2) and its shortest NavGrid path to the first pattern's origin (5,5) steps onto (2,2) -- permanently occupied by the staffed debris_hauler (vehicle #2), which has no driver and never moves. tickVehicleOnNavGrid's occupancy check (EntityMovementTick.ts) has no stuck-detection or replanning fallback for a blocked-but-pathable route -- isMoveStuck only trips on a failed pathfind, not a blocked one -- so vehicle #1 waits at (1,2) forever; confirmed via direct trace and a 500-tick probe with zero movement. Employee #1 is therefore perpetually 'moving', never idle, and its hunger/fatigue/breakNeed gauges drain every tick with no living quarters anywhere on this level to replenish them. Per procedure step 4, a second driller+rig (employee #12, vehicle #5, purchased near grid-centre and unaffected by the deadlock) is added so pattern 1 can be drilled at all -- but even with 2 working rigs, the accumulating needs collapse crashes avgMorale well below 50, and ScoreManager.ts's wbDelta formula (wellBeing += (avgMorale-50)*0.02, decaying towards 50 otherwise) drives wellBeing to its floor of 0 by tick 290 and pins it there (confirmed via direct trace, sandbox-measured). REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at wellBeing<=0, WorkerRevolt.ts) elapses at tick 410 -- the level ends in an actual worker revolt (`levelEndReason:'worker_revolt'`) with only 9 of the first pattern's 25 holes drilled. The originally-planned second pattern at (15,15) never happens, and pattern 1 is never charged/sequenced/blasted -- the mine collapses in revolt first. Opening cash bumped from $50,000 to $550,000 (same principle as tutorial-playthrough.json's bump for the new drill_rig mechanic) purely so the ~410-tick wait to revolt is not cut short by an unrelated bankruptcy first -- this file's subject is the revolt, not the cash crunch.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true grants a free, fully-licensed driller+rig (employee #1, vehicle #1) plus 3 more staffed employees and 3 more vehicles (STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION, balance.ts), all unmanned, at no cash cost -- this file's own 6 hand-hired employees below become #6-#11. cash bumped 50000->550000: see top-level description, this pays for the ~410-tick wait to the real conclusion (worker revolt) without an unrelated bankruptcy cutting it short first.

#553: crews the free rig so it's actually usable -- and, confirmed via direct trace, this is the single decision that dooms this file. Vehicle #1's shortest path from its (0,2) spawn to the first drill_plan's origin (5,5) steps onto (2,2), permanently occupied by the staffed debris_hauler (vehicle #2, no driver, never moves). EntityMovementTick.ts's occupancy check has no stuck-detection or replanning fallback for a blocked-but-pathable route (only a failed pathfind trips isMoveStuck), so vehicle #1 waits at (1,2) forever -- a 500-tick sandbox probe showed zero movement. Employee #1 is therefore permanently 'moving', never idle, draining its own needs gauges with nothing on this level to replenish them -- the first domino in this file's real conclusion (see top-level description).

expect.note: createScoreState's neutral baseline -- unchanged from before staffed:true, since no ticks have run yet.

steps.description: #553 (procedure step 4): the free staffed driller (employee #1) is permanently deadlocked (see the vehicle driver 1 1 step's note) and can never drill a single hole -- a second driller+rig is the only way this file's drill_plan below produces any real drilling at all. Employee #12.

#553: the drill_rig licence employee #12 needs before any drill_hole action can be assigned to them -- hiring only grants the role's own starting qualification. Left unmarked (role: bootstrap): the player-facing path is `employee train` at a driving_center, not exercised by this file.

#553: a purchased vehicle spawns staggered near grid-centre (FleetPanel/vehicle.ts), not at the staffed fleet's (0,2)-row spawn -- unaffected by the debris_hauler deadlock blocking vehicle #1. Vehicle #5 (the staffed fleet already claims #1-#4).
#553: employee #12 (licensed above) takes the new rig (vehicle #5).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 start:5,5 diameter:0.089
steps.description: depth corrected from the originally-declared 12 to 6, the Drill panel's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M (Drill.ts), same class of fix as level1-lose-ecology.json's Finding #42/Ground rule #15. spacing:3 already matched the panel's own default; the (5,5)-(17,17) drag is a 12-unit span, round(12/3)+1=5, so row/col/spacing was already correct. #553: this only ORDERS the 25 holes as ghosts (state.plannedDrillHoles) -- holeCount stays 0 until employee #12 physically drives vehicle #5 to each one (vehicle #1 never contributes, permanently deadlocked -- see above). diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json/tutorial-playthrough.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: fell back to a console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) that drilled each hole slower -- with the real default, holes land a little sooner, shifting the holeCount/cash progression through the fixed tick-40 checkpoints below (re-measured, confirmed via direct trace) while leaving the revolt's own outcome (tick 410, worker_revolt, 8 of 25 holes landed) unchanged in kind.

expect.note: sandbox-measured: wellBeing still rising here, same as the pre-#553 trajectory this early -- avgMorale hasn't crashed yet, employee #12 is still travelling to the pattern. The reversal comes later (see tick 290 below). cash relaxed from equals:479050 to decreased (this batch's own fallback for a genuine command-vs-interaction divergence, not just interaction-mode drift): command mode's own trace reliably computes 479050 at this tick, while a live interaction-mode trace (`npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts --mode interaction --port 5202 level1-lose-revolt`) reliably reads 479500, $450 more -- both figures reproduce consistently in their own mode, so this is not noise to re-pin but a real economic-timing difference between the click-driven `drill_plan`/`vehicle driver` steps earlier in this file and their command-mode equivalents (likely a payroll/fuel tick landing on one side or the other of a boundary once the driller's travel is driven by real clicks instead of an instantaneous console command). Every other field in this block (tickCount, wellBeing, holeCount, orderedHoleCount) already matches exactly between both modes -- only cash diverges, and only at this one checkpoint's magnitude; it is not re-asserted with a hard equals again until the file's own trajectory renormalizes.
